title_ar: الحج المبرور ليس له جزاء إلا الجنة
title_en: An Accepted Hajj Has No Reward but Paradise
body_ar: تحدث فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو في خطبة الجمعة عن فريضة الحج و الأشهر الحرم و فضل الحج و أن الله تعالى فرض الحج على عموم المسلمين فجعله فرضا مرتين : فرضا عينيا على كل مستطيع قادر مرة في العمر ، و فرضا كفائيا في كل عام على الناس أن يقام الموسم، و قد بين الله مناسك الحج لخليله إبراهيم و أمره أن ينادي في الناس بالحج فأسمع كل من يحج سواء منهم من كان ولد و من لم يولد فكان ذلك معجزة خالدة قال تعالى: (وإذ بوأنا لإبراهيم مكان البيت أن لا تشرك بي شيئا وطهر بيتي للطائفين والقائمين والركع السجود وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر يأتين من كل فج عميق ) كما تحدث فضيلته في الخطبة الثانية عن ما خص الله به يوم الجمعة من الفضل و أن الله هدى إليه هذه الأمة المحمدية و أضل عنه الأمم السابقة كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم " ثم هذا يومهم الذي اختلفوا فيه هدانا الله له "
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew spoke in the Friday sermon about the obligation of hajj, the sacred months, and the merit of hajj; and about how God the Exalted imposed hajj upon the generality of Muslims, making it an obligation in two ways: an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn) upon every person who is able and capable, once in a lifetime; and a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah) upon the people every year, that the season be held.

God made clear the rites of hajj to His intimate friend Abraham and commanded him to proclaim the hajj among the people, and He made every person who would ever perform hajj hear it — both those among them who had been born and those not yet born — and that was an enduring miracle. God the Exalted said: {And when We settled for Abraham the place of the House: associate nothing with Me, and purify My House for those who circle it, those who stand, and those who bow and prostrate; and proclaim the hajj among the people: they will come to you on foot and on every lean mount, coming from every deep mountain pass} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:26–27).

In the second sermon His Eminence spoke of the merit God has singled out for Friday, and of how God guided this Muhammadan community to it and let the earlier communities stray from it, as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Then this is their day, over which they differed; God guided us to it."

flags.arabic: الحج المبرور ليس له جزاء إلا الجنة
options: An Accepted Hajj Has No Reward but Paradise
A Hajj Performed Faultlessly Has No Recompense but Paradise
flags.note: The title is a prophetic report (al-Bukhari and Muslim), used by the site as a headline. It does not appear in the body, and the sermon as reported does not discuss it. مبرور covers both acceptance by God and performance free of sin and quarrel; 'accepted' is the usual English and is used here, with the alternative recorded.

options: making it an obligation in two ways
imposing it as an obligation of two kinds
flags.note: The distinction is the point of the sentence and the glossary terms are used exactly: farḍ ʿayn, binding on every individual able to perform it once in a lifetime, and farḍ kifāyah, discharged on behalf of all, here that the hajj season be held at all each year. The second is a less commonly stated formulation and should not be smoothed away.

flags.context: the second sermon, on the merit of Friday
options: let the earlier communities stray from it
led the earlier communities away from it
the earlier communities strayed from it
flags.note: Same construction as in record 872 of this slice, and the same uncertainty about the subject of أضل, except that here God is explicitly the subject of the parallel verb هدى in the same clause, which makes the first two readings the live ones. See the flag on 872.

translator_notes: A news report of a Friday sermon, not the sermon's text. Typed 'news' rather than 'khutbah' for that reason: nothing here is the Sheikh's own wording except the scriptural texts the report quotes.
The hadith in the last sentence is the same report quoted at greater length in record 872 of this slice, here in an abbreviated form. No narrator or collection is given in either record.
فج عميق rendered 'deep mountain pass'. Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
